member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.DataFormDateOptionsAttribute
member.summary: Provides attribute-level configuration of minimum date, maximum date, and date format for date editors within the .
member.remarks: This attribute customizes allowed date ranges and their format for a specific property in a DataForm model class. Set MinimumDate and MaximumDate as string representations, and optionally define a format string according to .NET date formatting patterns.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.DataFormDateOptionsAttribute.MinimumDate
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum date, as a string, that is allowed for selection in a date editor field within the DataForm.
member.value: A string representing the earliest selectable date. The default is string.Empty, which imposes no restriction.
member.remarks:
Set to an empty string (string.Empty) if you do not intend to limit the lower bound. The format must match the property. The restriction applies only if both MinimumDate and Format are provided. Usage example:
[DataFormDateOptions(MinimumDate = "22/01/2024", Format = "dd/MM/yyyy")] public DateTime? DateTimeValue { get; set; }

example.code: [DataFormDateOptions(MinimumDate = "01/01/2023", Format = "dd/MM/yyyy")] public DateTime? Birthday { get; set; }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.DataFormDateOptionsAttribute.MaximumDate
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum date, as a string, that is allowed for selection in a date editor field within the DataForm.
member.value: A string representing the latest selectable date. The default is string.Empty, which means no upper limit is enforced.
member.remarks:
Set to an empty string (string.Empty) if you do not intend to restrict the upper bound. The format must match the property. The restriction applies only if both MaximumDate and Format are provided. Usage example:
[DataFormDateOptions(MaximumDate = "22/02/2024", Format = "dd/MM/yyyy")] public DateTime? DateTimeValue { get; set; }

example.code: [DataFormDateOptions(MaximumDate = "31/12/2024", Format = "dd/MM/yyyy")] public DateTime? EndDate { get; set; }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.DataFormDateOptionsAttribute.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the date format string used to parse and values.
member.value: A representing the .NET date format pattern. The default value is based on the current culture's ShortDatePattern.
member.remarks:
Use standard .NET date format strings (e.g., "yyyy-MM-dd", "dd/MM/yyyy"). The format should correspond to how MinimumDate and MaximumDate are specified. If omitted, the system default short date is used. Usage example:
[DataFormDateOptions(MaximumDate = "22/02/2024", MinimumDate = "22/01/2024", Format = "dd/MM/yyyy")] public DateTime? DateTimeValue { get; set; }

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class with default values.
member.remarks: Defaults: and are set to empty strings (no limitation). is set to the active culture's short date pattern.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.FormGroup.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the is enabled.
member.value: true if the FormGroup is enabled; otherwise, false. Interaction with the form fields and their child components is disabled when the Enabled property is set to false. When set to true, the FormGroup and its child components become interactive. The default value is true.
member.remarks: The property provides a way to enable and disable the FormGroup and all its child components at runtime. This is useful for scenarios where certain sections of the form need to be disabled based on user input or business logic, such as progressive forms where later sections are enabled only after prerequisites are met. When the property is set to false, form field interactions such as input, focus, validation, and submission are prevented for the entire group. Enabling the FormGroup will restore full interactivity. This property affects all child FormItems and their associated editors but does not impact form-level events like submission until validation rules are satisfied. Ideal for conditional UI flows and preventing premature interactions.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.SfDataForm
member.summary: Provides a configurable and customizable data form for editing model values in Blazor applications. The automatically generates form items based on model property metadata, and provides support for templates, layout options, data annotations, and integrated validation.
member.remarks: The component is designed for rapid form development by automatically generating form fields for all properties in the given Model, or by allowing explicit configuration of form items for custom layouts and templates. The form integrates with EditContext and Blazor validation features, supports layout customization (column count, column spacing, floating labels), and exposes extensibility points such as custom buttons and validation message display. To use advanced features, define items through or use auto-generation. See the example for common usage.
member.example:
A simple example using to render a form for an Employee model:
<SfDataForm Model="@employee" ColumnCount="2"> <SfDataFormItem Field="FirstName" /> <SfDataFormItem Field="LastName" /> <SfDataFormItem Field="Email" /> <FormButtons> <SfButton Content="Submit" IsPrimary="true" /> </FormButtons> </SfDataForm>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.SfDataForm.AutoComplete
member.summary: Gets or sets the value of the autocomplete attribute of the component.
member.value: Accept the value.
member.remarks: on, the browser is allowed to automatically complete the input field based on the user's previous inputs. off, the browser is not allowed to automatically complete the input field. The autocomplete feature in the browser can be helpful in providing suggestions to users while they fill out the components. However, in certain scenarios, it might be necessary to disable this feature for security or privacy reasons.

examples.code:
<SfDataForm ID="MyForm"
             Model="@exampleModel"
                 Width="50%"
                AutoComplete="on" >
             <FormValidator>
                 <DataAnnotationsValidator></DataAnnotationsValidator>
             </FormValidator>
             <FormItems>
                <FormAutoGeneratedItems></FormAutoGeneratedItems>
             </FormItems>
            
             <FormButtons>
                 <SfButton>Submit</SfButton>
             </FormButtons>
             
             </SfDataForm>
            
             @code {
                
             public class ExampleModel
                 {
            
                     [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter FirstName here")]
                     public string FirstName { get; set; }
            
                     [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter LastName here")]
                     public string LastName { get; set; }
            
                     [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter Email here")]
                     public string Email { get; set; }
                 }
            
                 private ExampleModel exampleModel = new ExampleModel();

member.value: true if the Floating Label feature is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

remarks.para: When set to true, the Floating Label feature is enabled, causing labels to move to a floating position above the field when it is focused or contains user input, and it is enabled globally.
